summary.headline: August funnel numbers are inflated by a bulk import; win rate jumped to 85% even as revenue cooled for the season.
summary.body: HIH (52) and MQL (281) more than doubled MoM, but nearly 80% of new contacts arrived via an offline bulk import, not organic demand — SQL (126, +12.5%) and Opportunities (124, +9.7%) are the more reliable read. Revenue fell to $149.6K across 34 deals as the spring-summer district buying peak tapered into the August lull, but win rate improved sharply to 85% (from 56%), so deal quality held even as deal size shrank. MQA accounts stand at 12 in the buy window.

brand_lift.note: These are Google Search numbers, not social engagement — how often our brand and channels surface when people search. YouTube and Instagram are Search Console platform properties, visible in the Search Console UI but not exposed by the Search Analytics API, so those tiles stay blank rather than showing a fabricated zero. LinkedIn has no GSC connector — it's owned by Microsoft and isn't integrated with Google. ⏳ The week of Aug 31 is still provisional: Google has finalized only 5 of its 7 days, so its full-week total (303 branded clicks) is understated and will revise upward on the next run. The WoW figure shown compares the same 5 settled days in each week, which is the like-for-like read; the full-week comparison would be misleading until the week settles.

current.narrative: Lower-funnel conversion surge: SQL hit 31 (+138% WoW 🔥) and Opp 29 (+142% WoW 🔥) — the strongest lower-funnel week since late July, validating last week's forecast of a SQL rebound as the W35 HIH class began converting. HIH held at 17 (+6%) and MQL grew to 69 (+23%). Branded search provisional at 303 clicks for Aug 31 (+43% WoW on a matched 5-day window; week settles next run). Pipeline expanded to 32 district open deals (from 31) and held at 13 school deals. Enterprise led SQL and Opp with 15 entries each — consistent with an offline migration cohort moving down-funnel.

previous.narrative: This week's signal is a tale of two funnel halves: top-of-funnel strengthened meaningfully, with 16 High Intent Handraisers [HIH] entering — double last week's pace — and MQL volume held at 56, essentially flat. The lower funnel tells a different story: SQL entries dropped to 13 (from 33) and Opportunities to 12 (from 33), both at their lowest point in the trailing five weeks. The pattern is consistent with W34 pull-forward — end-of-month acceleration moved lifecycle entries that would otherwise have distributed into W35, so the dip is expected rather than alarming. Watch for SQL to recover toward 25–30 next week as the pipeline refills from this week's HIH surge.
